svg.text: The five archetypes of web vulnerabilities
Individual techniques keep multiplying; the shapes do not. Meeting a new one, first decide which cell it is in.
A. Boundary discrepancy – same bytes, two interpreters, different conclusions
Two components give different answers on how far one message or one value extends. Having no party to forcibly reconcile them is the web's structural condition (Part 01).
request smuggling (CL/TE) · cache poisoning and deception · reverse proxy path normalization bypass · mXSS · Unicode normalization differences · parser differentials generally
Shape of the defence: reduce to one interpreter (upstream HTTP/2), or reject ambiguous input rather than passing it on.
B. Identity discrepancy – the criterion for "who/what" splits in two
The criterion deciding access differs from the criterion that operates. The moment they come apart is the attack window.
CSRF (cookies by domain, SOP by origin) · DNS rebinding (name vs address) · X-Forwarded-For forgery (socket vs header)
trusting JWT kid/jku (the thing verified picks the verification key) · subdomain takeover (ownership of a name on cookie, CORS and redirect_uri allow lists moving)
Shape of the defence: fix the judging criterion as one, and keep input from changing it.
C. Missing privilege check – authentication once, authorization every time
Middleware handles whether someone is logged in, in one place, while "does this object belong to this user" has to be written per handler. Missing one is enough.
IDOR · BOLA / BFLA · mass assignment · forced browsing · validation done only on the client · missing field-level authorization in GraphQL
Shape of the defence: push authorization down to the data access layer and make the default "deny". Remove the places it can be forgotten.
D. Side-effect observation – learning it without reading it
The data itself is blocked and differences in response remain. The centre of gravity of 2020s research moved this way.
padding oracle · compressed length (CRIME) · blind/time-based SQLi · XS-Leaks · cache probing · Spectre · differences in redirect behaviour
Shape of the defence: make responses identical (constant time, uniform errors), or block the observation (process isolation, lower timer precision).
E. Resource asymmetry – the gap between the cost of sending and of processing
It holds with no vulnerable code. A combination of normal behaviours the spec permits creates the gradient of cost.
HTTP/2 Rapid Reset · ReDoS · abuse of GraphQL depth and aliases · XML bombs · compression bombs · unbounded pagination
Shape of the defence: cap processing cost, and charge the requester a cost for expensive operations too.
Questions on meeting a new technique: who interpreted what differently · which two criteria split · which check was missing · what was observed · who paid the cost
